archimate:Principle.name: batch
archimate:Principle.documentation:
CONTEXT
The Integration Layer Pilot proves three patterns on Azure Integration Services. For Batch, large volumes of data are moved on a schedule from a source system to a target using Azure Data Factory (ELT), and not through APIs or events.
Batch pipelines already exist example for SAHP and are in production. They transfer data from SAHP into the Data Platform using Data Factory. They are used today, so no new batch implementation is needed to prove the pattern.
What is not yet known is how these pipelines are set up, what documentation exists, and which standards they follow for documentation and scripts. Without that, a new batch feed cannot be built consistently.
PROPOSAL
Use the existing SAHP to Data Platform batch pipelines as the pilot's Batch pattern. No new pipeline is built.
The pilot will: - Review how the existing pipelines are set up, including structure, scheduling, error handling, monitoring and security. - Review the documentation and scripts that exist, and identify gaps. - Define standards for batch documentation and scripts, so future feeds are consistent. - Propose how a new batch feed can be implemented by reusing the existing pipeline design.
Why this option - The pipelines are in production, so the pattern is already proven in use. - Avoids building a duplicate pipeline for the pilot. - Reviewing and standardising brings the batch approach in line with the other two patterns. - Gives a repeatable template for new feeds.
Consequences - The pilot outcome for Batch is a review, standards and a reuse approach, not new code. - The result depends on access to the existing pipelines and their documentation, and on the time of the people who own them. - Gaps found in the documentation or scripts may need follow-up work outside the pilot.
Open points - Confirm the owner of the existing pipelines and agree access for the review. - Confirm what documentation and scripts exist.
Status: Proposed
